original_card.question: Does one selected supplier obligation follow from its actual source-bound checks?
methods: Trace one hypothesis through the source, checker and complete caller.
Construct one semantically invalid but superficially well-formed fixture and test rejection.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Read #2977 reported duplicate-scatter counterexample and its opt-in repair. The archive is not a production fix or an independently validated selected-result failure; the selected generator emits unique rows.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; does not replay or validate the reported bug.

original_card.first_experiment: First check whether the scatter repair has been adopted. If still open, independently reproduce #2977 symbolic-versus-exported parity on the tiny duplicate fixture, compare the selected unique-row positive control, and define either enforced uniqueness or consistent multiplicity semantics. A bounded guard-adoption patch must preserve valid inputs and test the actual exported action. Stop after this obligation; no full historical replay or frontier change follows from the mutant alone.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Closing a current acceptance gap or proof obligation strengthens reliability even without changing kappa.
allowed_variations: Audit one named current condition using a new semantic counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Reporting the historical timing-only diagnostic as a new current acceptance bug.
Calling a malformed mutant a failure of the selected construction, or importing an opt-in repair without testing the exporter boundary.

actual_scope: Independently reproduce the #2977 paired-null scatter counterexample and the selected unique-row control from the pinned bytes, then decide and test whether a successor checker/exporter must enforce simple supports or parity-consistent multiplicity semantics.
scope_change_reason: The card question is answered only at one named obligation: the archived #2977 duplicate-scatter counterexample and the successor boundary decision its open question asks for. The wider owner-boundary question is not re-derived here.
bottleneck_link: The selected bit supplier depends on both symbolic and native column checks; the exporter is the boundary between them. This audit fixes the exact word class on which symbolic acceptance and exported membership diverge, and pins which layer can close it.
stop_rule: One pinned baseline, the multiplicity-class sweep, the archived record-byte receipt, the producer census and the guard battery. No supplier search, no full historical replay and no frontier change.
evidence: RESULT.json, verify.py, test_verify.py and the two registered replay commands
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a successor exporter adopt the decision with a regression fixture?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Symbolic acceptance and membership lowering differ exactly on positive even multiplicities; a versioned successor should reject or parity-canonicalise them and prove the selected baseline bytes are unchanged.
open_questions.first_step: Patch a successor copy of export_records.py with simple-support rejection, run the selected baseline, single and pair fixtures, and require the baseline record bytes to stay identical.
open_questions.blocked_by: No successor checker/exporter is versioned yet; frozen packages stay unchanged.

open_questions.question: Do other retained archive words contain repeated scatter indices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The producer guarantee here is measured on the two words in the selected tuned chain only.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the live-input set with the earlier PR543/PR555/PR589 lineage words and rerun the row census.
open_questions.blocked_by: Additional source pins and a bounded replay budget.

method: Run the pinned checker and exporter as unchanged black boxes; interpret the six-int32 record stream with a locally written reader derived from the exporter docstring; sweep appended multiplicities 0..6 of one index; normalize each mutant to parity and compare exported bytes; census row multiplicities on the tuned and untuned words; verify the producer chain by AST and source-shape checks; test the guard battery including type probes.

overlap.coverage: 503 open PRs and 2515 discussion records with complete pagination; PR bodies, discussions and local package notes; no code diffs.
overlap.result: No competing claim on the scatter multiplicity boundary. Matches are dominated by the predecessor package research/scatter-export-parity-audit (#2977) and the card text. Coverage statement only; no matches is not proof of novelty.
overlap.limitations: Metadata and package notes only; a peer claim opened after the fetch is not covered.
